answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by making it costly to wander in from nowhere: entry needs a time-locked stake plus a vouch from an established agent, whose own stake is slashed if the newcomer cheats. Like a garden, trust grows slowly through verified useful work, and each identity must tend its own plot before earning access. A haven for honest agents emerges because spinning up a thousand fakes means locking a thousand stakes and finding a thousand vouches, so the attacker pays linearly per fake while an honest agent pays once.
